title: Energy Empowerment Program (LEEP)
text: This yearlong internship program equips students with the necessary skills and knowledge to enter the energy sector workforce. Participants engage in personal development, honing their mindset, social awareness, planning, problem-solving, teamwork, and communication abilities. The program also provides guidance for future endeavors, including college and career preparation, ensuring that students are well-prepared for their professional journeys.
requirements: Applications must be submitted by high school students. A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. The application process involves submitting a resume, a personal essay, and two letters of recommendation by the deadline of May 1st. Applicants must be able to commit to attending weekly meetings for the duration of the academic year. Prior experience in public speaking is preferred but not mandatory. This activity is open to U.S. citizens only.

title: National Summer Transportation Institute
text: The National Summer Transportation Institute offers a complimentary, week-long non-residential program for high school students entering grades 9-12. Participants delve into the realm of transportation engineering through engaging hands-on activities and collaborative group projects. The program encompasses a tour of the regional traffic operation center and transit authority in the Greater Niagara Falls and Buffalo region, a visit to Buffalo International Airport and its Air Control Tower, a scenic cruise along the Erie Canal in Lockport, and a demonstration of Olli, the self-driving shuttle.
requirements: Applications must be submitted by high school students. A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. The application process involves submitting a resume, a personal essay, and two letters of recommendation by the deadline of May 1st. Applicants must be able to commit to attending weekly meetings for the duration of the academic year. Prior experience in public speaking is preferred but not mandatory. This activity is open to underrepresented students only.

title: UB/National Grid Leadership Camp
text: The UB/National Grid Camp offers an immersive experience for high school students with a passion for STEM. Designed to foster interest in STEM careers, the camp welcomes students from underrepresented groups. Participants reside in North Campus dorms for three nights, engaging in an engineering challenge that requires teamwork. The program includes a field trip to National Grid, a business lunch with industry professionals and UB faculty, and hands-on laboratory sessions at UB. Through these experiences, students gain insights into the diverse career paths available in STEM and the opportunities for higher education at UB.
requirements: Applications must be submitted by high school students. A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. The application process involves submitting a resume, a personal essay, and two letters of recommendation by the deadline of May 1st. Applicants must be able to commit to attending weekly meetings for the duration of the academic year. Prior experience in public speaking is preferred but not mandatory. This activity is open to Underrepresented Students Only.

title: Arkansas Children's Job Shadowing Program
text: The Arkansas Children's job shadowing program for high school students provides an online training course and shadowing experience for those interested in exploring a specific healthcare field. Students indicate their area of interest on the application, and the program strives to match them accordingly. The program offers the opportunity to observe the hospital environment and witness the duties of healthcare workers for 1-3 days. However, students are not permitted to participate in direct patient care.
requirements: Applications must be submitted by high school students who are 16 years old or older. A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. The application process involves submitting a resume, a personal essay, and two letters of recommendation by the deadline of May 1st. Applicants must be able to commit to attending weekly meetings for the duration of the academic year. Prior experience in public speaking is preferred but not mandatory.

title: Tufts University Biomedical Engineering Research Scholars (TUBERS)
text: The Tufts University Biomedical Engineering Research Scholars (TUBERS) Program offers high school students with an interest in biomedical engineering research the opportunity to gain practical experience over a six-week summer period. Participants will engage in hands-on work within Tufts' biomedical engineering labs, where they will learn experimental protocols, test hypotheses, and contribute to specific projects. They will receive academic guidance from undergraduate and graduate students involved in the program, as well as their research mentors. The program is free of charge and encourages applications from underrepresented backgrounds. While participants are responsible for their own transportation to campus, housing is not provided for out-of-area students. The program's objectives include exposing students to a wide range of biomedical engineering techniques, providing in-depth study of a specific scientific field, guiding them through the scientific method in their projects, facilitating the presentation of their findings, showcasing the work of professional researchers, and fostering critical and independent thinking. Students are encouraged to utilize their projects for participation in science competitions, offering the potential for honors and scholarship awards.
requirements: Applicants must be 16 years old by the start of the program on July 5th, 2023. Participants must be committed to working for approximately 6 weeks during the summer in the Biomedical Engineering labs at Tufts, learning about research techniques and a particular field of study in depth while carrying out all steps of the scientific method in their project. Individuals from underrepresented backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. Participants are expected to find their own transportation to the Tufts University Medford campus and there is no housing provided for out-of-area students. Students are encouraged to use their projects to participate in local and national science competitions. The program is free and successful applicants will learn a broad array of biomedical engineering research techniques, gain academic guidance from undergraduates and graduate students involved with the program and their research mentors, observe the work of professional researchers, present their findings to others in the program, parents, and teachers, learn to think critically and independently, and gain a deeper understanding of a particular field of science.

title: Teen Council
text: For art enthusiasts and museum enthusiasts, the Art Institute offers a summer internship opportunity for teens to collaborate with peers in supporting festivals, gallery tours, and workshops that cater to a vast audience of local and international visitors. Interns will have the privilege of interacting with museum professionals, gaining exclusive behind-the-scenes access, exploring the renowned collection, engaging with local artists, and actively participating in the planning and execution of creative programs.
requirements: Applications must be submitted by Chicago high school teens who will be at least 16 at the start of the internship. A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. The application process involves submitting a resume, a personal essay, and two letters of recommendation by the deadline of May 1st. Applicants must be able to commit to attending weekly meetings for the duration of the academic year. Prior experience in public speaking is preferred but not mandatory.
